findings.where: Good for section: all twelve pills (First-time surfers, Remote workers, Long stays, Meeting people, Yoga, Nightlife, Budget, Cafés, Couples, Solo travellers, Scooter riders, Sunsets), desktop and phone
findings.fault: These are static facts, but they are built as filter chips: rounded pills with a fill and a 3:1 edge, laid out in a wrapping row like a filter bar. Some of them (Long stays, Meeting people, Nightlife, Couples, Solo travellers, Sunsets) are also in link colours. A visitor will expect tapping 'Remote workers' or 'Budget' to filter Canggu hostels, and nothing happens. Their fills vary for no reason, so some look 'selected' and others don't. A visitor can't tell whether the colours mean an on/off state, a category, or nothing.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on their phone comparing destinations would tap a chip that matches them, such as 'Solo travellers', to narrow things down. They'd get no response and decide the page is broken or still loading on a poor connection. This is on a product whose whole pitch is search and filtering.

findings.where: Vibe section heading, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The 'Vibe' heading is underlined, set in the link turquoise and italicised, so it looks like a link. The parts map shows it does nothing. The 'Surf' and 'Good for' headings around it are plain ink, so this one heading reads as the only link in the guide's body.
findings.who_objects: A visitor would tap it expecting more on Canggu's vibe, or vibe-filtered hostels, and get nothing. It also teaches them that underlines on this site don't reliably mean links.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank', footer 'How we rank', 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'Report content', and the MantaHostels wordmark in the nav
findings.fault: Each of these links points back to the page the visitor is already on, so they're dead. The wordmark, which is labelled 'MantaHostels home', also reloads this Canggu guide instead of going to the home page. 'How we rank' is the product's published-method trust claim, and it leads nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A wary first-time visitor checking how rankings work, or looking at the privacy policy or terms before trusting a pre-launch site, would click and land back on the same page. For a brand whose principle is 'trust is the product', that undercuts the trust. A visitor who taps the logo to get home gets nowhere.

findings.where: Nav 'Destinations' link (in the Menu panel on phone)
findings.fault: It points to #destinations on this page, but the page has no destinations section. The link scrolls nowhere and doesn't take the visitor to other destinations.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has read about Canggu and wants to compare Uluwatu or Lombok has no way onward. The site's only navigation to other destinations is dead.

findings.where: Coming-soon announcement block below 'What to look for', desktop and phone
findings.fault: The notice sits on a saturated red ground, which is the look reserved for errors and sold-out states. A plain 'listings coming soon' message therefore reads as an error or a failure alert. The parts map also flags the box and its text as possibly looking actable, but it does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scrolling to see hostels would read the red box as 'something went wrong' or 'Canggu is unavailable' rather than 'not launched yet'. On a phone with a poor connection, they could easily take it as a failed load.

findings.where: Page as a whole, end of the guide and announcement
findings.fault: The page has no action at all. Once the visitor has judged Canggu and learned that listings aren't live, the announcement offers nothing to do next. There's no way to find out when Canggu listings go live and no way on to another destination, and 'Destinations' is dead too. The page is a dead end.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next hop who has decided Canggu suits them is left with nothing to do on the site and will leave for another booking site.
